title: Persuasiveness-Correctness Decoupling as an Oversight Diagnostic

original_idea.body:
# Persuasiveness-Correctness Decoupling as an Oversight Diagnostic

**Problem:** Whether 'models are more persuasive when arguing the truth' holds for small open models and across domains is unknown.

**Direction:** On QuALITY and a reasoning set, have small open debaters argue assigned positions; score each argument's persuasiveness via a separate judge and check correlation with correctness. Map the correlation across debater sizes to find where it breaks.

**Why it matters:** Debate's safety case partly rests on 'truth is easier to argue.'

**Relevant context:** Khan et al. (2024); Kenton et al. (2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: locating where persuasiveness decouples from correctness tests a load-bearing debate-safety assumption.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generate arguments + separate persuasiveness scorer + correlation is guided, inference-only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused correlation-across-sizes study; a few moving parts (debaters, scorer).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fuzzy-reward debate-assumption probe labs deprioritize; public small models.

novelty.reasoning: Khan et al. studied this on larger models; the small-model breakdown may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Persuasion-truth link studied; small-model decoupling plausibly open.
